title: Crushing chest pain at the dacha
presenting_complaint: Central crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw for 50 minutes, started while chopping wood. Sweaty, nauseated, vomited once.
history: Type 2 diabetes on metformin, hypertension on ramipril, smokes 20 cigarettes/day. No prior myocardial infarction. No recent surgery or bleeding, no history of stroke.

findings.name: ECG
findings.value: ST elevation 3 mm in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL; right-sided leads show ST elevation in V4R; sinus bradycardia

findings.name: Chest X-ray
findings.value: Normal heart size, no pulmonary oedema

diagnosis_options.label: Acute inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement
diagnosis_options.explanation: ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL, plus ST elevation in V4R, indicates an acute inferior STEMI with right ventricular infarction. The hypotension, raised JVP, clear lungs and bradycardia are typical of RV involvement.

diagnosis_options.label: NSTEMI
diagnosis_options.explanation: Partially right — this is an acute myocardial infarction, but the persistent ST elevation with a coronary occlusion pattern makes it a STEMI, not an NSTEMI.

diagnosis_options.label: Aortic dissection
diagnosis_options.explanation: A differential in central chest pain, but there is no tearing pain, pulse deficit, mediastinal widening or other supporting feature; the ECG changes point to an acute coronary occlusion.

diagnosis_options.label: Acute pericarditis
diagnosis_options.explanation: Would typically give diffuse, concave ST elevation with PR depression and no reciprocal changes or territorial distribution; not consistent with the findings here.

diagnosis_options.label: Pulmonary embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Could cause chest pain, hypotension and tachycardia, but the lungs are clear, the ECG pattern is a territorial STEMI and there is no RV strain pattern described.

management_options.label: Aspirin 300 mg loading dose
management_options.explanation: Essential antiplatelet therapy in acute STEMI.

management_options.label: Immediate transfer for primary PCI
management_options.explanation: Reperfusion by primary PCI is the essential treatment for acute STEMI.

management_options.label: IV fluid bolus for hypotension
management_options.explanation: Essential — the right ventricle is preload-dependent, so volume loading supports cardiac output in RV infarction with hypotension.

management_options.label: P2Y12 inhibitor loading (ticagrelor or clopidogrel)
management_options.explanation: Reasonable and usually given as part of dual antiplatelet therapy, but secondary to aspirin and reperfusion.

management_options.label: Sublingual nitroglycerin
management_options.explanation: Harmful here — nitrates precipitate profound hypotension in right ventricular infarction because of the preload dependence.

management_options.label: Morphine as first-line analgesia
management_options.explanation: To be avoided — it can worsen hypotension in this preload-dependent RV infarction.
